cards.title: Interpretation of Renal Clearance and Urinary Recovery
cards.claim: Renal clearance (CLr) is calculated as the amount excreted unchanged in urine (Ae) divided by the plasma AUC over the same time interval. Low urinary recovery of unchanged drug does not definitively exclude renal contribution to total clearance if the assay lacks specificity for unchanged analyte, if the collection interval is incomplete, or if systemic dose context is missing.
conditions: Applicable when assessing the contribution of renal vs. nonrenal pathways to total clearance.
Requires paired plasma and urine data from the same subject over identical time intervals.
Requires validated assay specificity for the unchanged analyte to distinguish from metabolites.
required_inputs: Plasma concentration-time data for AUC calculation.
Urine concentration and volume data for Ae calculation.
Assay validation data confirming specificity for unchanged drug.
Complete urine collection intervals matching plasma sampling windows.
limitations: Low recovery of unchanged drug in urine does not prove absence of renal elimination if metabolites are not accounted for or if assay specificity is poor.
A low urinary recovery result from one compound or study is not a universal renal-clearance rule.
Renal insufficiency models in animals may not directly translate to human dose adjustment recommendations without clinical validation.
cards.downstream_use: Use to determine if renal function is a significant covariate for clearance. If CLr is negligible relative to total CL, renal dose adjustment may not be required, but this must be confirmed with human data.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Renal/nonrenal clearance, nonlinear elimination, formulation and route limits

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
